title: The Nephites believe the prophets
summary: No living Nephite doubted the prophets’ words. The people knew Christ had come because of the signs and things already come to pass, and knew the prophets’ words would be fulfilled.

explicit_facts.text: No living soul among the Nephites doubted the words of the holy prophets; they knew those words must be fulfilled.
They knew Christ had come because of the signs that had been given and the things that had already come to pass; they knew all things would come to pass according to what had been spoken.

unspecified_visual_details: The people's appearance, clothing, ages, and precise setting.

narration.text: there was not a living soul among all the people of the Nephites who did doubt in the least

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses report the people's knowledge and conviction, not a visible appearance of Christ or a gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ appearing, the people gathering, or a specific location.

title: Serving God
summary: They forsake their sins, abominations, and whoredoms, and serve God diligently day and night.

explicit_facts.text: They forsook their sins, abominations, and whoredoms.
They served God with all diligence day and night.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People engaged in service to God, without specifying its form.
unspecified_visual_details: Their location, clothing, and the form of their service.

narration.text: Therefore they did forsake all their sins, and their abominations, and their whoredoms, and did serve God with all diligence day and night.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a location or specific worship rite, or depict the forsaken sins as events.

title: Prisoners and preaching
summary: The people imprison captured robbers, preach God’s word to them, and release those who repent and covenant not to murder again.

explicit_facts.text: All robbers were taken prisoner; none escaped unless slain.
The prisoners were put in prison and taught the word of God; those who repented and covenanted not to murder again were freed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A preacher addressing prisoners within a prison; release may be represented at the prison threshold if all actions remain one moment only.
unspecified_visual_details: The prison’s appearance, the preacher’s identity, and the means by which the repentant prisoners are released.

narration.text: did cause the word of God to be preached unto them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: If depicting a single visual moment, choose the preaching to prisoners; release is a subsequent reported action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the deaths or invent the preacher’s identity or words.

title: Condemned and punished according to the law
summary: Those who did not enter into a covenant, continued to have secret murders in their hearts, and were found threatening their brethren were condemned and punished according to the law.
characters: Those who did not enter into a covenant and were found threatening their brethren

explicit_facts.text: Some did not enter into a covenant.
They continued to have secret murders in their hearts and were found breathing out threatenings against their brethren.
They were condemned and punished according to the law.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, the people administering the law, and the form of punishment are not specified.

narration.text: were condemned and punished according to the law.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports these events; it does not describe a particular sentencing or punishment scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify authorities, depict a specific punishment, or portray secret thoughts as visible actions.

title: The combinations ended
summary: The account says the wicked secret combinations came to an end.

explicit_facts.text: The wicked, secret, abominable combinations that involved much wickedness and many murders were ended.

unspecified_visual_details: The manner in which the combinations ended and any people or place that might be shown.

narration.text: they did put an end to all those wicked, and secret, and abominable combinations

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse summarizes an outcome; do not create a new event depicting it.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a confrontation, leader, or visual symbol for the combinations.

title: Twenty-five years
summary: The twenty-second through twenty-fifth years pass, completing twenty-five years.

explicit_facts.text: The twenty-second, twenty-third, twenty-fourth, and twenty-fifth years passed; twenty-five years had passed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained passage-of-time device, such as a calendar or changing dates.
unspecified_visual_details: The calendar system, seasons, and events during those years.

narration.text: and thus had twenty and five years passed away.

prohibited_inventions: Do not add events to the passing years.

title: A limited record
summary: The narrator says many marvelous things happened during the twenty-five years, too many to include, though records contain the proceedings and Nephi gave a shorter true account.

explicit_facts.text: Many things happened over twenty-five years; not even a hundredth part could fit in the book.
Other records contain the proceedings, and Nephi gave a shorter true account.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A book or record may be shown to convey the narrator’s comments about what can be written.
unspecified_visual_details: The records’ physical appearance and the unrecorded events.

narration.text: this book cannot contain even a hundredth part
a shorter but true account was given by Nephi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are comments about the record, not depictions of the unrecorded events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict unspecified marvelous events or place Nephi physically in this scene.

title: Mormon describes his record
summary: Mormon’s narration identifies Nephi’s record as his source and states that the plates for his own record were made with his own hands.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator's record follows the record of Nephi, which was engraved on the plates of Nephi.
The narrator states that he makes the record on plates he made with his own hands.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, recording tools, and plates’ appearance are unspecified.
The narrator’s physical appearance and age are not described.

narration.text: Therefore I have made my record of these things according to the record of Nephi, which was engraven on the plates which were called the plates of Nephi.
And behold, I do make the record on plates which I have made with mine own hands.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Attribute narration to Mormon (old), using the established character label and supplied narrator identification; these verses do not independently name him or establish his age.
Present this as a narratorial statement about the record, not a newly staged record-making event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nephi as physically present.
Do not stage the reported creation of the plates or invent their manufacturing process.
Do not turn the narratorial account into a new present-tense recording scene.
Do not infer physical age or appearance from the established character label.
Do not add identifying words to the quotations.

title: Mormon identifies himself
summary: Mormon gives his name and says he is a disciple of Jesus Christ, called to declare Christ’s word among his people.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says he is named after the land of Mormon, where Alma established the first church among the people after their transgression.
Mormon says he is a disciple of Jesus Christ, called to declare his word so his people might have everlasting life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown writing or speaking as narrator.

narration.text: I am a disciple of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The account mentions Alma and the first church historically; neither is necessarily physically present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Alma establishing the church in this scene.

title: The purpose of the record
summary: Mormon says he makes a record in accordance with God’s will, concerning the prayers and faith of holy ones, from Lehi’s departure from Jerusalem to the present.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says it became expedient, according to God’s will, to make a record so the prayers of departed holy ones might be fulfilled according to their faith.
He describes it as a small record from the time Lehi left Jerusalem until the present.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon recording, with no visual depiction of the departed holy ones.
unspecified_visual_details: The holy ones’ identities and appearance, and the record’s setting.

narration.text: a small record of that which hath taken place

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi’s departure is a time reference, not a present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lehi, Jerusalem, or departed holy ones as physically present.

title: Accounts and eyewitness record
summary: Mormon says he used earlier accounts until his own day, then recorded what he saw; he calls his record true, notes that some things cannot be written, and ends his personal remarks.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon made his record from earlier accounts until the beginning of his day, then recorded things he had seen himself.
He calls his record just and true and says many things cannot be written in their language.
Mormon ends his personal remarks and proceeds to his account of prior things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon with his record, in a moment of writing.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular things he witnessed and the setting.

narration.text: then I do make a record of the things which I have seen with mine own eyes.
I know the record which I make to be a just and a true record

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize the record-making process; do not depict unspecified events Mormon witnessed.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the beginning of Mormon’s day or the prior events as a new scene.

title: Mormon blesses God
summary: Mormon identifies himself as Lehi’s pure descendant and blesses God and Jesus Christ for bringing their fathers from Jerusalem and giving his people knowledge. He says God has blessed Jacob’s house, shown mercy to Joseph’s seed, and blessed obedient children of Lehi.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon identifies himself as a pure descendant of Lehi and blesses God and Jesus Christ for bringing their fathers out of Jerusalem and giving his people knowledge unto salvation.
Mormon says God blessed the house of Jacob and showed mercy to the seed of Joseph.
He says God blessed and prospered the children of Lehi when they kept his commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown in reflection or prayer while recording.
unspecified_visual_details: Mormon’s posture, setting, and the appearance of the historical people mentioned.

narration.text: I have reason to bless my God and my Savior Jesus Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The bringing of the fathers from Jerusalem is recalled, not depicted as happening now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Lehi’s journey or portray God or Jesus Christ in an appearance not described.

title: Promises of gathering
summary: A remnant of Joseph’s seed will be brought to knowledge of the Lord. Jacob’s scattered remnant will be gathered, the covenant with the house of Jacob will be fulfilled in due time, and they will know Jesus Christ and be gathered to their own lands.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will again bring a remnant of Joseph’s seed to knowledge of the Lord their God.
The remnant of Jacob’s seed is scattered across the earth and will be gathered from its four quarters.
The covenant with the house of Jacob will be fulfilled in due time, restoring them to knowledge of that covenant.
They will know their Redeemer, Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and be gathered to their own lands.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and appearance of any narrator.
The timing, appearance, and specific lands of those to be gathered.

narration.text: And then shall they know their Redeemer, who is Jesus Christ, the Son of God;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses promise future events; they do not narrate a gathering taking place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the gathering as occurring in this scene.
Do not invent a visible narrator or an appearance for a divine figure.
